title: Offline producer-claims revoke runs against a live daemon, whose in-memory claims can overwrite it
wanted_capability: Revoking a producer scope claim should either be an online daemon operation (operator-authenticated admin route or MCP tool that updates the in-memory store and rebuilds producer auth) or the offline CLI should take the daemon lifetime lock like project-catalog retire does. Today the offline command writes the claims file while the daemon keeps the claim in memory: the claim stays effective until restart, and the daemon's next claim persist rewrites the revoked record back.
fallback_used: Ran the offline revoke inside the pod immediately before a converge that restarted the daemon, so the restart loaded the revoked file.
